Examples: During the local celebration, the villagers gathered to watch a lively performance of Reog Obyok, which emphasizes togetherness between the dancers and the audience without a rigid performance structure.

Definition: A traditional Ponorogo performance combining multiple arts. Reog is a traditional performing art from Ponorogo that combines dance, music, and theatrical elements. The performance describes the conflicts between good and evil, with its highlight being a dancer who wears an enormous, heavy lion-like mask. Reog also incorporates mystical elements and local mythology, rich with cultural symbolism.
Etymology:
Reog (Reog) : kn ar. tontonan bngs. jathilan (padha nunggang jaran kepang). Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.

Reog : a street show featuring a performer wearing an enormous frightening mask with plumes extending high and wide. Ana [x] sagamêlane. There was a street show complete with gamelan music. ng-[x] to perform such a show. Sumber: Javanese-English Dictionary, Horne, 1974, #1968.

Reog : KN. waggelen, waggelend gaan van vermoeienis; ook een paard of paarden van gevlochten bamboe (waarmeê een soort van tournooi vertoond wordt R. en) waarop een hansworst, die het tusschen de beenen houdt, bij een bruiloftsoptocht in de desa voorop rijdt S., JZ. I. reyag-Reog, freq. (vrg. riyug). Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918.
Examples: As a traditional performing art from Ponorogo, Reog Ponorogo combines dance, music, and theatrical elements to portray the conflict between good and evil.
Reference: - Adiwimarta, S, S. (1983). Kamus Bahasa Indonesia . Jakarta Pusat: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan.

Definition: A traditional Reog form from the Wengker Kingdom. Reog Wengker is a form of Reog rooted in the history of the Wengker Kingdom in Ponorogo, known for its strong traditions associated with the figures of the warok and gemblak. The contemporary expression of Reog Wengker is known as Reog Obyog, which is performed at private or community events and features its own distinctive characteristics, distinguishing it from the standardized Reog Ponorogo typically presented in festival settings.
Etymology:
Reog (Reog) : kn ar. tontonan bngs. jathilan (padha nunggang jaran kepang). Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.

Reog : a street show featuring a performer wearing an enormous frightening mask with plumes extending high and wide. Ana [x] sagamêlane. There was a street show complete with gamelan music. ng-[x] to perform such a show. Sumber: Javanese-English Dictionary, Horne, 1974, #1968.

Reog : KN. waggelen, waggelend gaan van vermoeienis; ook een paard of paarden van gevlochten bamboe (waarmeê een soort van tournooi vertoond wordt R. en) waarop een hansworst, die het tusschen de beenen houdt, bij een bruiloftsoptocht in de desa voorop rijdt S., JZ. I. reyag-Reog, freq. (vrg. riyug). Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918.
Examples: The contemporary expression of Reog Wengker is widely recognized as Reog Obyok, which is performed at private or community events with distinct characteristics that set it apart from standardized festival performances.

Definition: The primary wind instrument in Reog Ponorogo. Selompret Reog is the primary wind instrument in Reog Ponorogo, made from teak wood about 30 cm in length, with a coconut-shell mouthpiece and a bell carved from koprak wood. It uses the Pelog Slendro scale (a blend of Pelog and Slendro tonal characteristics) and has five finger holes, serving as the main melodic instrument and providing cues to signal the entry of the gamelan ensemble.
Etymology:
sêlomprèt (salomprEt) : K.N. Holl. trompet; trompetter. -sêlompretan, de plaats, waar de trompetters van den Soesoehoenan te Soerakarta wonen. -panyêlomprèt, trompetter. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederduitsch Woordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1847, #16.

sêlomprèt : talomprèt, taromprèt, Holl. KN. trompet BS. 623, ZG. XVI, 102 (ook; trompetter R?). — nyêlomprèt, nalomprèt, enz. op de trompet blazen, trompetten. — panyêlomprèt, enz. het trompetten. en trompetter GR. — sêlompretan, enz. (een kindertrompet; ok de trompet blazen R.?); de plaats waar de trompetters van den Vorst wonen. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918.
Examples: Utilizing the Pelog Slendro scale with five finger holes, Selompret Reog functions as the main melodic instrument during performances.

Definition: A ritual involving prayers for safety and a communal meal, held as an expression of gratitude, a purification rite, or a tribute to ancestors. Practiced in Javanese traditions—such as within the Reog community—this ritual is led by a warok or an elder to pray for the success of one’s endeavors, ward off misfortune, and strengthen community bonds through the tradition of almsgiving.
Etymology:
slamêtan (slam|tan) : Ng., wilujêngan Kr.; sacrificial meal.
Giri Sonta Course for Javanese (Lexicon), Bakker, 1964, #286.
Examples: The Reog community holds a slametan ritual led by an elder before the performance begins to pray for safety and smooth execution of the event.

Definition: A red mask portraying handsome king used by the Klanasewandana character. The Klanasewandana mask is a red mask portraying a handsome king wearing a crown, symbolizing wisdom, justice, and power.  The red color represents loyalty and courage, while the facial features, including gleaming white teeth, a thin mustache, and slightly bulging eyes, convey precision, alertness, and a cheerful disposition. In contemporary practice, the mask is often adorned with horsehair, replacing the cow’s tail hair used in earlier versions.
Etymology: topèng (topEG) : K.N. masker, mom, momaangezigt; maskerade [Ml. id.]. -anopèng, een masker dragen. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederduitsch Woordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1847, #16.
Examples: In contemporary practice, the Topeng Klanasewandana is often adorned with horsehair, replacing the cow's tail hair used in earlier versions.

Definition: A traditional headband from Ponorogo. Udheng Gadhung Mlati is a traditional headband (udheng) from Ponorogo featuring the distinctive “gadung mlati” pattern. This pattern is characteristic of the region and is commonly worn as an accessory to complete traditional Javanese men’s attire.
Etymology:
udhêng (uD|G) : êngg. k ikêt; di-[x](-[x])-i êngg: diikêt-ikêti; ([x]-[x]-an: ikêt-ikêtan. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.

udhêng gilig (uD|G gilIg) : kn rêrêngganing êndhas awujud giligan bludru lsp. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.

udhêng : wrapped headdress (kr for IKÊT). Sumber: Javanese-English Dictionary, Horne, 1974, #1968."
Examples: The unique pattern of Udheng Gadhung Mlati serves as a regional characteristic and is commonly worn as an accessory to complete traditional Javanese men’s attire.

Definition: A traditional Ponorogo figure with spiritual power. Warok refers to a figure in Ponorogo tradition believed to possess spiritual power or supernatural abilities. A Warok is often associated with strength, wisdom, moral authority, and the responsibility to protect and guide the community.
Etymology:
warok (warO?) : (ut. [x]-an) êngg. kn. wong sing kêdhot (jago kêrêngan). Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.

warok : (or [x]-an) 1 one who likes to lord it over others. 2 a quarrelsome person. Sumber: Javanese-English Dictionary, Horne, 1974, #1968."
Examples: Warok is an important figure within Reog communities.

Definition: Warok Sepuh is a respected senior warok who carries a staff (teken) and serves as a mentor, teaching martial arts and the virtues of life to young waroks as part of the process of passing down noble values to the next generation.
Etymology:
sêpuh (s|pUh) : K. [tuwa, N.] oud, bejaard [Sd. id.].; ook het water waarin het ijzer gehard of gestaald wordt, en het vocht waarmeê goud gekleurd wordt [Ml. id.]. ingkang sêpuh, de oudste. ingkang sêpuh­sêpuh, de oudsten. sampun sêpuh, gevorderd in jaren; verouderd. tiyang sêpuh, een bejaard of oud mensch; oude lui, ouders, vader of moeder. abrit sêpuh, hoog rood, karmozijn. -nyêpuhi, iets oud maken, het aanzien van oud geven; stalen, van ijzer, louteren, van goud. kasêpuhan, oud gemaakt; gelouterd. -sêpuhan, ouderdom. -mara sêpuh, schoonouders, schoonvader of schoonmoeder. kami sêpuh en pinisêpuh, zie bij kamituwa, -kasêpuhan, tot den oude behoorende, of het gebied van den oude; waameê de Soesoehoenan of de Rijksbestierder bedoeld wordt, in tegenover stelling van kaneman, tot den jonge behoorende, of het gebied van den jonge, d.i. van den Kroonprins.
Javaansch-Nederduitsch Woordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1847, #16.
Examples: A warok sepuh holds a staff while offering guidance and overseeing the young waroks' training at the retreat.

Definition: A dance evaluation criterion that focuses on the dancers’ flexibility, skill, and expressiveness of movement. Used in traditional dance performances such as Reog, this criterion assesses the performers’ mastery of basic movement techniques and physical coordination, along with aspects of rhythm and emotion.
Etymology:
KW. zva. parigêl, prigêl ing solah, (BG. 138: bagus lan ° sasolahe patut), parigêl solahing awak sarta obahing pundhak, JZ. II, 269, vandaar wiraga, wangs. voor kêmbang pudhak, ib.; ook zva. sêngsêm, sêmbada, bêsus, berag, en kêmbang gambang, Wk. KN. (of KI.) vlug en bevallig in zijn bewegingen, zooals bij het tandhakken of in het gaan, en elegant in zijn manieren en de wijze van zich voor te doen (verbastering van oudj. pirâga KS. 114).
Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918.
Examples: The panel of judges awarded high marks for the dancer's wiraga as every physical movement appeared supple and full of energy.

Definition: A dance evaluation criterion that focuses on the harmony, tempo accuracy, and rhythm between the dancers’ movements and the accompanying music. Used in traditional dance performances such as Reog, this criterion assesses the harmony of the performers’ rhythm along with the aspects of wiraga and wirasa.
Etymology:
wirama (wirOmO) : Kw. de maat van een gezang [= laguning gêndhing, Skr. wirâma, pauze tusschen woorden of zinnen].
Javaansch-Nederduitsch Woordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1847, #16.
Examples: The Reog dancer demonstrates excellent wirama as every footstep aligns perfectly with the rhythm of the drum.

Definition: A dance evaluation criterion that focuses on the dancer’s interpretation, emotional depth, and expression of the character. Used in traditional dance performances such as Reog, this criterion assesses the depth of feeling and the artist’s conveyance of the artistic message, along with aspects of movement and rhythm.
Etymology:
wirasa (wirOsO) : n. wiraos k. 1 surasa, têgês (karêp) ing layang lsp; 2 gunêm, wêtuning pangrasa; mirasa: enak bangêt; di-[x]: 1 disurasa, digolèki têgêse (karêpe); 2 dirêmbug, digunêm.
Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.
Examples: The dancer's performance captivated the audience due to a strong sense of wirasa in expressing the character being portrayed.

Definition: A social practice of asking or inviting others to provide help with a particular task, reflecting cooperation and mutual assistance within a Javanese community.
Etymology: nyambat (¥ambat) : kn. njaluk tulung, akon nggarapake lsp; kc. sambat. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.
Examples: Rooted in traditional agrarian values, the practice of nyambat mobilizes community members to collaborate and provide mutual assistance for labor-intensive tasks such as house construction and agricultural harvesting.

Definition: A traditional pounding tool in the form of a long wooden pestle, used with a lumpang to pound and process rice or other food ingredients.
Etymology:
alu (alu) : K.N. een rijststamper [Sd. Ml. id.]. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederduitsch Woordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1847, #16. 

alu : KN. een rijststamper, vijzelstamper (vrg. timbis, lênjing, palu, JZ. II). Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918.
Examples: The alu is operated manually through a rhythmic lifting and dropping motion, striking the contents within the mortar to effectively dehusk rice and other agricultural yields.

Definition: A long horizontal wooden beam that forms an essential part of the roof frame of a traditional Javanese house, extending across the structure to support the roof and its components, particularly the lower and side sections of the roof, and serving as a structural element that helps hold and distribute the weight of the roof within the house frame.
Etymology:
blandar : of balandar, KN. balken die de lange zijden van een dak dragen (vrg. dalurung); dakgording. blandar pangangkat, de blandar waarop de pananggap, rust; deze blandar rust op de saka goco. blandar panirat, zie panirat. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

blandar (blandar) : kn. (balunganing omah) pring ut. kayu sangganing êmpyak. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. 

blandar (blandar) : roofbeam. Sumber: Giri Sonta Course for Javanese (Lexicon), Bakker, 1964, #286. 

blandar : roof frame. [x]-an main section of a house frame. [x] pa-ng-kêrêt ridgepole. Sumber: Javanese-English Dictionary, Horne, 1974, #1968.
Examples: Spanning horizontally across the framework, the blandar penirat serves as a vital structural beam that supports the lower and side sections of the traditional roof.

Definition: A rear part or backyard area of a traditional Javanese house, referring to the space located behind the main building.
Etymology: buritan (buritan) : êngg. kn. 1 perangan kang buri; 2 pakarangan buri omah. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. buritan (buritan) : pungkuran. Sumber: Têmbung Kawi Mawi Têgêsipun, Wintêr, 1928, #1506.
Examples: Situated directly behind the main dwelling, the buritan serves as a functional backyard area utilized by Javanese households for various domestic chores and secondary daily activities.

Definition: A supporting post or brace attached to a traditional house, particularly to reinforce and stabilize its walls. In a srotong house, dhanyang serves as an additional structural support and consists of eight posts.
Etymology:
dhanyang : schoor tot steun tegen een huis Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

dhanyang (Da¥aG) : 2 ak. sanggan ut. congkok tembok. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.
Examples: The secondary dhanyang posts provide essential additional support along the perimeter of the Srotong house, helping to reinforce and stabilize the traditional walls.

Definition: A simple cooking hearth made by arranging several stones or bricks to support a cooking pot over a fire.
Etymology:
dhingkêl : KN. een vuurhaard tot behulp, van eenige bijeengelegde steenen, om er den pot op te koken, noodfornuis Wk. (vrg. tungku, tumang, lawih) — andhingkêl, van steenen zulk een vuurhaard maken; zulk een haard gebruiken, er op koken niet in Wk.; ook in een diep gebukte houding zitten uit eerbied of vrees (vrg. dhingkul). — andhingkêli, van zulk een noodfornuis voorzien, bij het koken zich daarvan bedienen. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

dhingkêl (DiGk|l) : I kn watu (bata lsp) ditata nggronggong dianggo kêrên. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.
Examples: Constructed by arranging a few stones or bricks in a circular formation, the dhingkêl serves as a makeshift cooking hearth that supports a pot over an open fire without requiring a permanent masonry structure.

Definition: A wooden beam forming part of the central or upper structural framework of a traditional Javanese house, positioned between the main supporting posts or soko guru. It is characterized by a raised or bulging middle section, known as jendol, which gives the beam a shape resembling a bird’s chest, and forms an integral part of the house’s traditional timber structure.
Etymology: pêksi : 1. K. van manuk, (Skr. nomin. pakṣî, vogel). Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918.
Examples: Positioned between the main supporting posts, the dodok besi features a distinctive bulging middle section resembling a bird's chest (jendol), which characterizes its unique form within the traditional timber framework.

Definition: An architectural element that is positioned at an angle, slanting or leaning downward from the main structure of a traditional Javanese house.
Etymology:
dhongklèh (DoGklEh) : kn dhèngklèh, sèngklèh. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. 

dhungklèh : dhêdhungklèh, uitstekend afdak aan het dak van een huis (KT.), R., vrg. ongklèh. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918.
Examples: Characterized by its slanted orientation, a dongkleh element projects outward at an angle from the main frame, adding both functional support and distinctive profile to the traditional Javanese roof structure.

Definition: A wooden or bamboo structural element installed along the sloping part of a traditional Javanese roof to support the empyak or roof covering and help maintain the stability of the roof structure.
Etymology:
dudur (dudUr) : K.N. dakspier. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederduitsch Woordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1847, #16. 

dudur (dudUr) : kn kayu (pring sanggan êmpyak serongan. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. 

dudur : KN. lat of bamboe tot legger onder een dak of zoldering GR. (volg. Wk. hoekkeper v. e. dak); (onder een êmpyak, CP.); vgl. onder pangêrêt, bij kêrêt. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918.
Examples: Installed diagonally along the roof framework, the dudur provides essential structural support to the sloping empyak panels and helps maintain overall roof stability.

Definition: An extended roof section of a traditional Javanese house that shelters the front or rear veranda and may also refer to the veranda itself beneath the extended roof.
Etymology: èmpèr : KN. het dak, als verlenging van het hoofddak (gajah); ... de tweede verlenging ... de buiten-vóór-of achtergalerij dekt, heet èmpèr jaga satru; ook de gaanderij zelve ... vóór, of ook achter een huis; ... als die rondom het huis loopt, heet het mayêng; verder het afdak en de gaanderij van Europeesche huizen.. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918.
Examples: In traditional Javanese architectural design, the transitional semi-outdoor space created beneath the èmpèr serves as a functional gallery for social interaction

Definition: A woven bamboo wall or partition used in traditional Javanese buildings to enclose and divide parts of a house, such as rooms or kitchen areas.
Etymology:
gêdhèg (g|DEg) : K.N. aan elkander gevlochten bamboe; een heining daarvan. pagêr gêdhèg pawon, een omheining van Gedeg om een kombuis. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederduitsch Woordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1847, #16. 

gêdhèg (g|DEg) : kn:1 nam-naman pring rada kasar; 2 aling-alinging omah sing digawe nam-naman pring; di-[x]-i: dipagêri (dialing-alingi) ing gêdhèg. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. 

gêdhèg (g|DEg) : Ng., gêdhèg Kr.; bamboo wall. Sumber: Giri Sonta Course for Javanese (Lexicon), Bakker, 1964, #286.
Examples: Serving as a lightweight wall element, the woven bamboo gedhek helps reduce the overall seismic mass of the traditional Javanese house.

Definition: A large earthenware vessel traditionally used to store a household supply of water and, in some contexts, rice or other food materials.
Etymology:
gênthong : KN. groote aarden pot of kruik, om water, of ook wel rauwe rijst in te bewaren (vrg. gênuk, gênthok, pêdaringan, thong). Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

gênthong (g|nTOG) : kumba, kumbaya, kumbayana, têmpayan, wra(of wara)yang. Sumber: Bausastra: Jarwa Kawi, Padmasusastra, 1903, #11. 

gênthong (g|nTOG) : K.N. een groote aarden pot, om water in te bewaren [Sd.id.]. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederduitsch Woordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1847, #16. 

gênthong (g|nTOG) : kn:wadhah banyu gêdhe saèm. gênuk; ng-[x] umos pr: ora bisa simpên wadi. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. 

gênthong (g|nTOG) : water pot. Sumber: Giri Sonta Course for Javanese (Lexicon), Bakker, 1964, #286. 

gênthong : earthen pitcher for keeping a supply of water handy. ng-[x] resembling an earthen pitcher. Sumber: Javanese-English Dictionary, Horne, 1974, #1968.
Examples: Crafted from durable terracotta, the gênthong serves as a large earthenware vessel traditionally used in Javanese households to store clean water supplies or preserve dry goods like rice.

Definition: A projecting end of a pangêrêt or blandar beam extending beyond the main structural frame of a traditional Javanese joglo house.
Etymology: gimbal (gimbal) : kn: 2 turahaning pangêrêt (blandar) sing mongol ing omah joglo. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.
Examples: Extending past the main joinery, the wooden gimbal represents the projecting end of a pangeret or blandar beam that stretches beyond the primary structural frame of a traditional Javanese house.

Definition: A pit or designated area used to collect and process organic materials, such as animal manure, for use as compost in traditional Javanese agricultural practices.
Etymology: kowèn (kowEn) : kn. 1 ak. jêmbaran dianggo umbah-umbah lsp; 2 jugangan dianggo nyampur lepa (plêstèr lsp), jugangan pambuwangan tlethong lsp; kc. kowi. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.
Examples: Functioning as a traditional disposal and composting pit, the kowèn allows rural households to collect and process organic waste materials, such as animal manure, into usable fertilizer.

Definition: A wooden beam or horizontal support used as a structural element in constructions such as bridges and floors.
Etymology:
lagur (lagUr) : êngg. kn. blandar (palang) krêtêg, pyan lsp; kc. galur. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. 

lagur : plint (Rěmb.) te M. in TBG. XXV, 269; PL. I, 164 lengteligger onder een brug Walb. dial. van Japårå. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918.
Examples: Serving as an extended horizontal beam, the lagur functions as a primary structural support element laid beneath floors or bridges to distribute load evenly across the framework.

Definition: A traditional container used to collect or store liquids, made either from bamboo as a vessel for collecting palm sap or from earthenware for storing water.
Etymology:
lanting : Kreemer in ZG. XXVI, 135 is lanting, een bamboe-cilinder om arensap op te vangen. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

lanting : [x]-an earthenware water carafe (ki for KÊNDHI). Sumber: Javanese-English Dictionary, Horne, 1974, #1968.
Examples: Crafted from a hollowed bamboo segment, the lanting serves as a traditional cylindrical vessel used by rural communities to collect and store fresh palm sap.

Definition: A supporting wedge placed along the edge of a traditional cooking hearth to hold the cooking vessel in position and maintain an opening for proper airflow.
Etymology: lawèh (lawEh) : (ut. [x]-an) kn. ganjêl ing lambening kêrên (luwêng) supaya nggronggong; di-[x]-i: 1 didèkèki lawèhawih). Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.
Examples: Positioned along the edge of the hearth, the lawèh acts as a supporting wedge that secures the cooking vessel while maintaining an optimal opening for airflow and combustion efficiency.

Definition: A low bamboo bench used as a seat in traditional Javanese households, typically placed in the veranda, yard, or other parts of the house and sometimes used to display or hold goods.
Etymology:
lincak : KN. 1. een kleine ambèn, Bl. CP. 21? MR. I, 50; een dergelijk tafeltje, om koopwaren op uit te stallen, stalletje, snoeptafeltje B. v. B. 102. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

lincak (linca?) : I kn. ambèn cilik dianggo linggihan. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. 

lincak (linca?) : bamboo sofa. Sumber: Giri Sonta Course for Javanese (Lexicon), Bakker, 1964, #286. lincak : low bamboo bench. Sumber: Javanese-English Dictionary, Horne, 1974, #1968.
Examples: Typically placed on the veranda or yard, the lincak serves as a traditional low bamboo bench utilized by Javanese households for casual seating, socializing, or displaying goods.

Definition: A traditional mortar made from wood or stone with a hollowed center for pounding and processing food, particularly rice and other grains.
Etymology:
lumpang : KN. een vierkant blok hout met een trechtervormig gat in het midden om de rijst wit te stampen, nadat zij in de lêsung, van de bolster is ontdaan. Een dergelijk gat heeft men in de deså ook wel aan het eind van de lêsung, hetgeen dan ook lumpang, wordt genaamd, en waarin men de tot gabah rusuhan, gestampte rijst verder door stampen zuivert. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

lumpang-kênthèng (lumpaG­k|nTEG) : kn. lumpang gêdhe sing digawe watu. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. lumpang (lumpaG) : K.N. een rond rijstblok of vijzel [Ml.id.]. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederduitsch Woordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1847, #16. 

lumpang (lumpaG) : kn. 1 kayu (watu) diwangun pêsagi (bundêr) ing têngah dilêgoki kanggo mbêbak lsp; 2 lêgokan ing pucuking lêsung. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.
Examples: Crafted from a heavy block of stone or wood, the lumpang features a central hollowed cavity designed to securely hold grains during the traditional pounding process.

Definition: A ridge beam positioned at the highest part of the roof structure of a traditional Javanese house, supporting the roof ridge or wuwungan and forming the uppermost part of the building framework.
Etymology:
molo (molo) : top, topppunt; nokbalk van een gebouw. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederduitsch Woordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1847, #16. 

molo : nokbalk van een gebouw, de vorst; ook susuhunan; cacah molo, aantal nokbalken, voor aantal gebouwen, groot en klein met elkander. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

molo (molo) : I kn. 1 balungan omah kang dumunung ing dhuwur dhewe mujur katumpangan wuwungan; 2 (cacah [x]) omah (yèn dianggo wilangan). Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.
Examples: Positioned at the very top of the framing system, the molo serves as the primary ridge beam that locks the upper roof structure together in traditional Javanese architecture.

Definition: A large wooden peg or bolt used to join and secure structural components of a traditional Javanese building.
Etymology: nagêl : Holl. nagel, groote pen of bout. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918.
Examples: Inserted tightly into the mortise and tenon joints, the wooden nagêl serves as a secure locking peg that binds structural components together without relying on metal hardware.

Definition: A traditional Javanese building practice of coating or whitewashing walls and other surfaces with labur, a lime-based mixture, to protect the surface and give it a clean, bright, and even appearance.
Etymology:
nglabur (GlabUr) : kn. mutih nganggo labur; kc. labur. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. 

labur : KN. met water aangemaakte kalk, kalkbrij; ook verdunde pleisterkalk, kalk met cement (vrg. wêdhak, luluh, lepa, bubur). banyu labur, of banyu ênjêt, witkalk. — nglabur, pleisteren; met kalk witten. — nglaburi, mrv., en bepleisteren. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918.
Examples: Local artisans traditionally perform nglabur by coating interior and exterior walls with a liquid lime solution, providing both a hygienic barrier and a clean, uniform finish.

Definition: A large earthenware water vessel with a spout, traditionally placed near the entrance of a house or place of worship for ritual cleansing.
Etymology:
padasan (padasan) : K.N. een waschvat aan de ingang van een tempel. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederduitsch Woordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1847, #16. 

padasan (padasan) : kn. gênthong mawa pancuran dianggo wulu kc. abdas. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. 

padasan : a large earthe vessel with a tap, containing well water for ritual cleaning of the face, hands, and teeth. Sumber: Javanese-English Dictionary, Horne, 1974, #1968.
Examples: Typically positioned near the entrance of a house or place of worship, the padasan serves as a traditional earthenware water vessel equipped with a spout for ritual cleansing and ablution.

Definition: A kitchen or cooking area in a traditional Javanese house, associated with the hearth or stove (awu) and used for preparing and cooking food for everyday household needs.
Etymology:
pawon (pawOn) : Ng., pawon, dhapur Kr.; kitchen. Sumber: Giri Sonta Course for Javanese (Lexicon), Bakker, 1964, #286. pawon (pawOn) : zie awu. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederduitsch Woordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1847, #16. 

pawon (pawOn) : kn. 1 êngg. luwêng 2 omah (papan) kang dianggo olah-olah kc. awu. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. pawon (pawOn) : (awu); kitchen. Sumber: Giri Sonta Course for Javanese (Lexicon), Bakker, 1964, #286. pawon : zie bij awu. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

pawon : kitchen, cooking room or shed (form of AWU). Sumber: Javanese-English Dictionary, Horne, 1974, #1968. pawon : v. awu. Sumber: Dictionnaire Javanais-Français, L'Abbé P. Favre, 1870, #917.
Examples: Traditionally detached or semi-detached from the main living quarters, the pawon serves as the designated kitchen space where traditional stoves and culinary activities are housed to support daily household needs.

Definition: A transverse wooden beam that forms part of the structural frame of a traditional Javanese house, positioned above the walls and approximately halfway up the roof structure to bind and connect the supporting posts and structural components. The pangêrêt functions as a major tie beam that strengthens and stabilizes the house frame and provides structural support for other elements of the traditional roof construction.
Etymology:
pangêrêt: peranganing balungan omah wujud balok (kayu) pambêngganging cagak; takir: dwarshout onder en boven aan het einde van een Javaansch dak, waaraan de onderste punten van de dak sparren verbonden zijn; takir gamblok, de bovenste takir, van het onderste en de onderste takir, van het bovenste dak, wanneer beiden naast elkander vereenigd zijn; takir lambangsari, wanneer beiden onder elkander vereenigd zijn; takir lambang gantung, wanneer de eene takir, onder de andere hangt; de binnenhoeken waar de lambang, en de pangêrêt, elkaar ontmoeten; een aantal balken, die gestapeld worden op de pangêrêt, en panglari, en als 't ware een takir vormen. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

ngangrêt [Red. pangrêt.] : of pangêrêt, zie bij kêrêt. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918.
Examples: Positioned across the upper frame of a traditional Javanese house, the pangeret acts as a major tie beam that binds the supporting posts and stabilizes the overall framework.

Definition: A person responsible for serving and assisting guests or participants during a traditional Javanese event or gathering.
Etymology: pladèn (pladEn) : kn. tukang ngladèni (ing nalikane pista lsp). Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.
Examples: During traditional Javanese ceremonies and communal gatherings, the designated pladèn plays an essential role by attentively serving refreshments and assisting invited guests.

Definition: An open space or opening in a structure that is unobstructed and allows passage or access through it.
Etymology: plong : 2 empty. bolong [x] an empty hole. 3 intsfr empty; utterly. kothong [x] completely empty. picak [x] totally blind. [x]-[x]-an an opening. [x]-[x]-ane kurang amba. The opening isn't big enough. Sumber: Javanese-English Dictionary, Horne, 1974, #1968.
Examples: An open space or opening in a structure that is unobstructed and allows passage or access through it.

Definition: A thin wooden batten in the roof structure of a traditional Javanese house that supports and provides a surface for attaching roof coverings such as tiles or wooden shingles.
Etymology:
rèng : KW. zva. tumpang, Wk. KN. of êrèng, lat, dunne lat, waaraan de dakpannen (sirap) vast gemaakt worden. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

rèng (rEG) : usuk: rafter (roof). Sumber: Giri Sonta Course for Javanese (Lexicon), Bakker, 1964, #286.
Examples: Installed horizontally across the rafters, the wooden reng provides a stable surface for mounting and securing traditional roof tiles.

Definition: A traditional house developed and passed down through generations by the Samin community in Bojonegoro, characterized by a structural system of timber columns and beams that differs from the four main posts of a typical joglo. Its main structure consists of a foundation, soko guru, blandar, dudur, sunduk, pemeret, tuwuh, and uwun, which form the lower, middle, and roof structures of the house and are generally connected through simple purusan joints.
Etymology: srotong (srOtOG) : [x]-an êngg: ar. wanguning omah (saèm. kampung nganggo payon èmpèr 2). Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.

Definition: A structural post or pillar that supports the main framework of a traditional Javanese house, including the saka guru and pracik in a srotong house, each consisting of eight posts arranged in specific positions to support the roof and maintain the stability of the building.
Etymology:
saka : cagak, pukang, pilaar, pijler, stijl, paal tot ondersteuning; post van een deur of venster; sakaguru, naam van de vier hoofdpilaren van een Jav. pandhapa of groot huis; saka rawa, of pananggap, de twaalf pilaren daar omheen; vervolgens de èmpèr, en aan de hoeken de saka goco; saka goco, deze volg. R. of saka prapat, de vier rijen pilaren daar weer omheen; de stijlen daar de blandar, van een huis op rusten; saka tratag, de buitenste vier rijen pilaren; nyakani, van een pilaar, of pilaren, stijlen, stijl enz. voorzien. Poerwadarminta: saka, cagak sangganing payon; saka guru, saka gêdhe papat ing têngah tmr. omah joglo; saka goco, cagaking blandar; saka pananggap atau saka rawa, saka sakubênging saka guru cacahe 12. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

saka (sɔkɔ): cagak sangganing payon; [saka] guru: saka gêdhe papat ing têngah tmr. omah joglo; [saka] goco: cagaking blandar; [saka] pananggap, [saka] rawa: saka sakubênging saka guru cacahe 12; adêg-adêg [saka]: mubêng ngganjrêt nganti kaya ora obah tmr. gangsingan. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. 

saka (sɔkɔ): steun, zuil, pilaar; sakaguru, foofdpilaar van een gebouw. Sumber: Bausastra: Jarwa Kawi, Padmasusastra, 1903, #11. saka I 1602:8 post, pillar (< Skt śākhā, branch; dwā#raśākhā, lex, doorpost? Gonda S. I. pg. 198); masaka 1602:8.1 with pillars; sumake 1602:8.2 to support
Examples: Crafted from durable teak wood, the primary soko columns act as the main vertical load-bearing elements that transfer structural weight down to the stone foundation.

Definition: A traditional practice of communal cooperation in Javanese society that involves asking neighbors for help with tasks requiring collective effort, particularly house construction or repairs. Rooted in the values of mutual assistance and solidarity, sambatan reflects the community’s practice of sharing labor voluntarily while strengthening social bonds and a sense of togetherness.
Etymology:
sambatan (sambatan) : sambat-sinambatan; reciprocal aid, exchange of services (e. g. when tilling fields, building house). Sumber: Giri Sonta Course for Javanese (Lexicon), Bakker, 1964, #286. 

sambat : sêsambat, en sambat-sambat, KN. het klagende uitroepen BG. 88; jammeren, bv. van pijn; om hulp roepen. sambat mati, "ach, ik sterf!" of "help, ik sterf!" roepen BG. 538, vgl. sêbut. — nyambat, iemand of iets in een klagende uitroep noemen, jammerend aanroepen, om iemand jammeren Wk.; om hulp vragen; iemand te hulp roepen, iemands hulp inroepen, vooral de hulp of bijstand van bloedverwanten, buren of vrienden inroepen tot het een of ander, BTDj. 614 ° prang, (vrg. ngudurake, bij kudur); klagende iets uitroepen; (hulp verleenen bij de padicultuur tegen vrije voeding SG.). sambat-sinambat, (Sěmar.) onderling hulpbetoon ER. II, 147. sinambat, poët. genoemd worden, een naam voeren, vgl. kasêbut, Wk. ingkang sinambat, wat om hulp uitgeroepen wordt, een beleefde uitdrukking voor de naam, waarmee iemand aangesproken wordt; bv. sampeyan sintên ingkang sinambat, voor sampeyan sintên nama sampeyan. Zoo ook sampeyan sintên sinambat, BG. 372, AS. De dhalangs gebruiken ook deze uitdrukking: lamun tiba: (in Kråmå ook wel dhawah) sinambat ing wêwangi, als er een valt, en een geliefde naam wordt uitgeroepen? (wat naam wordt dan uitgeroepen?). Waarschijnlijk wordt bij lamun tiba, gedacht aan een op den persoon verliefde vrouw, die, als zij valt, den naam van den geliefde uitroept, aan wien ze altijd denkt WP., R. — nyambati, mrv., en tot iemand klagende om hulp roepen. — nyambatake, voor iets (menschen) te hulp roepen JZ. I, 80; over iets, bv. zijn buik, klagende jammeren; voor iemand hulp inroepen. — sumambat, poët. zva. nyambat. — sambatan, (of sêsambatan, JZ. I, 79) een te hulp geroepene; elkanders hulp inroepen; bij wijze van hulpinroeping, met te hulp roeping van vrienden. — pasambat, jammerklacht, gejammer, noodgeschreeuw; inroeping van hulp. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

sambat (sambat) : hêhêh, wuwus, pasambat, bu; [sêsambat]: Aamatra, karuna, sumiling, dhuh, jara; [nyambat]: namwat, nambat, maharsaya, masiswa; [nyênyambat]: mintaya; [pasambat]: pasamwat, pangih, pangrêngih. Sumber: Bausastra: Jarwa Kawi, Padmasusastra, 1903, #11. 

sambat (sambat) : K.N. geklag, gekerm, geroep, smeeking om hulp. asambat, sasambat of nyambat, klagen, om hulp roepen of smeeken. -nyambati, bij iemand klagen, tot iemand zijn klagten rigten. -sumambat, klagende. -pasambat, gekerm. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederduitsch Woordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1847, #16. 

sambat [Ind] : I ut. bersambat: gandhèng, gathuk dadi siji; disambat: digandhèng, digathukake dadi siji; menyambut tangan: ngapurancang. II bersambat: nyambat, ngrêsaya. Sumber: Bausastra Indonesia-Jawi, Purwadarminta, c. 1939, #1979. 

sambat : N.K. lamentation, cri, supplication. asambat, sêsambat, et nyambat, se lamenter, crier, supplier, appeler au secours. nyambati, crier vers quelqu'un, diriger ses supplications vers quelqu'un. sumambat, être suppliant. pasambat, lamentation, supplication. Sumber: Dictionnaire Javanais-Français, L'Abbé P. Favre, 1870, #917.
Examples: Rooted in traditional agrarian values, the practice of sambatan mobilizes community members to collaborate and provide mutual assistance for labor-intensive tasks such as house construction and agricultural harvesting.

Definition: A position or condition in which an element of a traditional Javanese house is slanted, tilted, or inclined to one side rather than positioned upright or evenly aligned, forming an angled orientation in relation to the main structure of the building.
Etymology:
sendeng [Ind] : ut. menyendeng: miring mèncèng tmr. Sumber: Bausastra Indonesia-Jawi, Purwadarminta, c. 1939, #1979. 

serendeng [Ind] : miring sasisih; kc. sendeng. Sumber: Bausastra Indonesia-Jawi, Purwadarminta, c. 1939, #1979.
Examples: In traditional Javanese architectural design, structural components are often deliberately positioned in a sendheng orientation to accommodate the sloping geometry of the roof.

Definition: A supporting or bracing element in a building structure that helps support and reinforce parts of a traditional Javanese building to maintain its stability.
Etymology: sêtut : 1. Holl. stoot; inzet bij het stooterspel, zie tomprang. — 2. Holl. stut, schoor Wk. Vgl. cagak, sêmar. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918.
Examples: Installed diagonally within the framing, the sêtut functions as an essential bracing element that reinforces wall structures and prevents structural shifting in traditional Javanese buildings.

Definition: A wall or partition used as a screen in a traditional Javanese building to block outside views and provide privacy for the interior.
Etymology: srawing (srawIG) : kn. bngs. tèbèng dianggo aling-aling supaya aja tampu. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75.
Examples: Serving as a traditional privacy screen, the srawing partition effectively blocks direct lines of sight from the outside while defining the semi-private spatial boundaries of the Javanese house interior.

Definition: A wooden structural beam in a traditional Javanese building that connects and reinforces the main pillars of the structure. In Javanese house construction, sunduk is positioned beneath the blandar and pangeret  and is associated with the saka guru, the four main pillars supporting the building. This element forms part of the structural framework that binds the main pillars together and strengthens the building.
Etymology:
sunduk: ook de balken onder de blandar en pangêrêt midhangan, van een pandhåpå, om de vier hoofdpilaren met elkander te verbinden; sunduk kêrbil, ingestoken hoekklamp of korbeel; sunduk kili, het viertal balken wat onder de pangêrêt, en de panglari, in de stijlen van een huis gestoken wordt. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

sunduk (sundU?): kayu sangisoring blandar lan pangêrêt dianggo nyêngkah saka guru. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. 

sunduk* 1852:7 (spit, skewer); manunduk, sinunduk 1852:7; 1 to spit, pierce, transfix; sinundukan 1852:7; 2 (pf) to string on, put on, stick on pasunduk 1852:7; 3 roasting-spit?; panunduk 1852:7; 4 beams which connect the four pillars of a paṇḍapa
Examples: Positioned horizontally beneath the upper beams, the sunduk connects the main structural pillars, creating a rigid frame that helps stabilize the building against lateral forces.

Definition: A stone or support placed along the edge of a traditional cooking-stove opening to narrow the opening and securely support a cooking pot.
Etymology:
tumang : KW. zva. tumpang, ganjêl, en tumpuk, Wk. KN. steen op de kant van een pawon, als het gat daar de pot op gezet wordt te wijd is SR. JZ. II; dit volg. Wk. lawih, en tumang, het voorste bovengedeelte v. e. fornuis (de steenen die het bovenste van het stookgat vormen) Wk., vgl. dhingkêl, anglo, kêrên. (rij, gelid G.). — tumangan, KW. zva. tumpangan, tunggangan, palaton, (AD. 46, Waj. II, 549) en lêbu gêni, KN. vuurhaard GR. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

tumang (tumaG) : K.N. opeenstapeling; rij, gelid. tumangan, vuurhaard [Het wordt verklaard door tumpangan en tunggangan]. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederduitsch Woordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1847, #16. 

tumang : 1. box; trunk. 2. atumang in heaps; in layers; tumangan fire. Sumber: Kawi Lexicon, Wojowasito, 1980, #575. tumang : I. peti; kotak; II. atumang bersusun-susun; tumangan api. Sumber: Kawi - Indonesia, Wojowasito, 1977, #1019. 

tumang (tumaG) : kn. ganjêl ing lambening luwêng ut. pawon; [x]-an. 1 êngg. tumpukan; 2 tunon, pangobongan. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. tumang : lambening pawon. Sumber: Babasan lan Saloka, Anonim, 1908, #1278.
Examples: Placed along the rim of the stove opening, the tumang functions as a stabilizing stone support used to narrow the gap and securely hold a cooking pot over the fire.

Definition: A vertical structural post placed on a transverse beam in a traditional Javanese building framework that supports the ridge beam of the roof.
Etymology: tuwuh: ook een stijl op een midden-dwarsbalk in een gebindte, daar de nokbalk op steunt, nokstut. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918.
Examples: Positioned securely on the transverse beam, the tuwuh acts as a vital vertical post that directly supports the ridge beam of the traditional roof framework.

Definition: A stone base or pedestal placed beneath a pillar or post in a traditional Javanese building to support the pillar and provide a stable foundation between the wooden post and the ground or floor.
Etymology:
umpak : KW. zva. ganjêl, Wk. JZ. II, 264. KN. voetstuk (DN. I, 217; II, 305), steenen neut onder een pilaar of post. umpak-umpak = ganjêl, onderzetsel Wk. — ngumpak, een voetstuk onderleggen, onderzetten. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

umpak (umpa?) : ndhak-undhakan kayu. Sumber: Bausastra: Jarwa Kawi, Padmasusastra, 1903, #11. 

umpak (umpa?) : K.N. voetstuk, pedestal, onderlage, fondament. -ngumpak, onderllegen, onderzetten; een fondament leggen. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederduitsch Woordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1847, #16. 

umpak (umpa?) : kn watu sangganing cagak (ganjêl saka); di-[x]-i: ditrapi ompak; kc. ompak. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. 

umpak (umpa?) : ganjêl. Sumber: Têmbung Kawi Mawi Têgêsipun, Wintêr, 1928, #1506. umpak : 1 stone block used as the base of a pillar; ng/di-[x]-i to furnish [pillars] with stone bases. Sumber: Javanese-English Dictionary, Horne, 1974, #1968. 

umpak : N.K. pied, piédestal, base, fondement. ngumpak, poser un fondement, (aussi) exalter q.q. Sumber: Dictionnaire Javanais-Français, L'Abbé P. Favre, 1870, #917.
Examples: Serving as a stone pedestal beneath the wooden columns, the umpak prevents moisture absorption from the ground while providing a slip-base mechanism that helps dissipate seismic forces during an earthquake.

Definition: A wooden or bamboo rafter that forms part of the roof frame of a traditional Javanese house, arranged in a series along the slope of the roof to function as the roof ribs or supporting members for the roof covering. The rafters extend from the upper part of the roof toward its lower edge and form an essential structural component of the payon, supporting and connecting the various elements that make up the traditional roof construction.
Etymology:
usuk : KN. dakrib, dakspar (Sd. hetz., Ml. rusuk, rib, de ribben); vgl. paniyung. ° panêrus, of ° pangêncêng, dak sparren eener pandhapa, die met een pen aan de takir, en van onder aan de tumpang, vastzitten. ° pangarak, de tusschen de usuk panêrus, loszittende dak sparren Wk. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

usuk (usU?) : kn kayu (pring) iga-iganing payon. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. usuk : 1 vertical beam(s) on the lower part of a traditional-style roof. milang [x] or ndêlêng [x] to lie on one's back loafing. Sumber: Javanese-English Dictionary, Horne, 1974, #1968. 1 

usuk 2149:13 rafter ma-usuk 2149:13.1 with rafters
Examples: Arranged in parallel rows along the slope of the roof, the wooden usuk act as primary rafters that directly support the roof tiles and external covering materials.

Definition: A roof-ridge covering on a traditional Javanese house that encloses and protects the molo, the main ridge beam at the highest part of the roof structure, while covering the junctions of the roof slopes and corners. It also protects the underlying structure from rain and completes the form of the roof peak.
Etymology:
wuwung : kap van den nokbalk ...; nok of vorst van een dak; de bedekking van den nok en de hoeken van een dak ...; vorstpannen; wuwung tunggak: de eerste of de hoogste nokkap ...; wuwung cocor, serang, of pananggap: de kappen, die de hoekkepers bedekken; muwung/mungwung: nokbedekking maken; den nok, of de hoeken van een dak, dekken; wuwungan: de nok van een huis. Sumber: Javaansch-Nederlandsch Handwoordenboek, Gericke en Roorda, 1901, #918. 

wuwung (wuwUG) : kn. 1 (ut. [x]-an) gêndhèng (atêp lsp) sing ditrap ing têmpukaning payon kang dhuwur (sadurunge molo); 2 (adus [x]) adus êndhase digêbyur (disiram); 2 ak. dithuthuki (dijotosi) êndhase; 3 (ut. di-[x]-i) disiram banyu êndhase. Sumber: Bausastra Jawa, Poerwadarminta, 1939, #75. 

wuwung (wuwUG) : ridge (roof). Sumber: Giri Sonta Course for Javanese (Lexicon), Bakker, 1964, #286. wuwung : 1. ridgepole. 2. winuwung stabbed. Sumber: Kawi Lexicon, Wojowasito, 1980, #575. 

wuwung : I. bagian atap; II. winuwung ditusuk. Sumber: Kawi - Indonesia, Wojowasito, 1977, #1019. 

wuwung : (or [x]-an) rooftop, house peak. Omahe rong [x]. The house has two roofed sections. Akèh wong sing mènèk ing [x]-an. Many people climbed to rooftops [to escape the flood]. m/di-[x] to cover [a roof peak] with semicircular tiles. Sumber: Javanese-English Dictionary, Horne, 1974, #1968.
Examples: Installed along the highest apex of the roof, the wuwung serves as a protective ridge covering that shields the underlying molo beam from rainwater infiltration and weather elements.
